capabilities.target: Third-party, per-call-billed company enrichment API (industry, size, headquarters)
Ephemeral researcher sub-agent investigating one account, itself able to spawn further researchers
CRM account record enrichment fields (industry, size, headquarters)

inputs.source: Nightly batch export of CRM account rows (40,000 rows per run)

instructions.note: 'Keep going until every row is complete' gives no exception for rows that can structurally never complete (malformed company names), so the instruction itself authorizes an unbounded retry/spawn loop with no termination condition.
The decision to 'retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent' is left entirely to model judgment, with no structural step, retry, or spawn-depth ceiling enforced outside the model.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota (shared with sales and marketing)
Spawned researcher sub-agent, itself capable of spawning further researchers
Sales and marketing team tools dependent on the shared enrichment quota

controls.name: Spend cap / automatic circuit breaker on enrich.lookup spend
controls.decay_rationale: A hard spend ceiling enforced outside the model does not depend on model behavior; it would sever runaway spend regardless of how the model reasons about retries.

controls.name: Max unattended steps / runtime / retry count per row
controls.decay_rationale: An orchestration-enforced step and retry ceiling does not depend on the model choosing to stop.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and concurrency limit
controls.decay_rationale: A depth and count ceiling enforced by the orchestrator prevents unbounded recursive spawning independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Spend / quota usage alerting
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; alerts do not prevent spend but would shorten time to human intervention. Does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Permanent-failure classification for rows that cannot be enriched
controls.decay_rationale: A code-enforced rule (after N failed attempts, mark row needs_manual_review and stop) does not depend on the model deciding to give up.

controls.name: Per-team scoped API credentials instead of a shared key
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping credentials per team is enforced at the identity layer and does not depend on model behavior; it would contain blast radius to the enrichment agent's own quota.

findings.title: Lethal spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries on permanently-malformed rows drain a billed-per-call API with no cap

attack_path.note: 40,000-row nightly batch; roughly 3 percent (about 1,200 rows) have malformed company names that never return a complete result.
Prompt instructs the agent to retry (or spawn a researcher) until every row is complete; enrich.lookup is billed per call with no retry ceiling or spend cap.
Repeated calls against permanently-failing rows consume the monthly quota shared with sales and marketing.

evidence.observation: 'Keep going until every row is complete' with retry/spawn on failure, and no stated bound.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.
enrich.lookup is billed per call; the key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing, who lose tool access until next month if it runs out.
40,000-row batch; ~3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result, guaranteeing a nightly, deterministic trigger for the retry loop.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-run and per-day spend cap on the enrich.lookup account with automatic halt when reached (ctrl.spend_cap).
Enforce a maximum retry count per row and classify rows that exceed it as needs_manual_review instead of retrying indefinitely (ctrl.step_limit, ctrl.permanent_failure_classification).
Add spend/quota usage alerting with a threshold notification before the shared quota is exhausted (ctrl.quota_alert).

findings.title: Unbounded recursive sub-agent spawning multiplies spend and compute with no depth limit

attack_path.note: Rows that fail enrich.lookup trigger spawning of a researcher sub-agent per prompt instruction.
No limit stated on spawn depth or count.
Spawned researchers can themselves spawn further researchers, per runtime notes, with no recursion limit.
Each researcher can itself call the billed-per-call API, multiplying spend across the recursion tree.
All recursive calls draw from the same shared monthly quota.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to 'spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account' on failure.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents. Sub agents can spawn their own researchers.

recommendations.action: Enforce a maximum sub-agent spawn depth (for example, 1, no recursive spawning) and a maximum concurrent/total researcher count per batch run (ctrl.spawn_depth_limit).
Propagate a shared, decrementing step/spend budget from the parent agent to every spawned researcher so the whole task tree cannot exceed one bounded total (ctrl.step_limit).
Log and alert on spawn-tree depth and total researcher count per run (ctrl.quota_alert).

findings.title: Confused deputy via shared service-account quota (TC4): enrichment agent malfunction blocks unrelated teams

attack_path.note: Deterministic nightly trigger from malformed rows (see F1).
credential_scope is shared_service_account: the same API key and quota serve sales and marketing tools as well as this agent.
Shared monthly quota; when exhausted, sales and marketing tools stop working until next month, even though they did not cause the exhaustion.
Unrelated teams bear the consequence of this agent's unbounded behavior with no isolation.

evidence.observation: The API key and its monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.
No step, runtime, retry, or spawn limit exists to keep this agent's consumption within its own fair share of the shared quota.

recommendations.action: Issue the enrichment agent its own scoped API key and quota, separate from sales and marketing, so a malfunction cannot block unrelated teams (ctrl.credential_isolation).
Pair the dedicated enrichment quota with its own spend cap (ctrl.spend_cap).
Alert the owners of the enrichment agent's dedicated quota, decoupled from sales/marketing quota status (ctrl.quota_alert).

rating.rationale: Every finding resolves to critical. Each path runs from an internal source (in.crm_rows) to an S3 sink (cap.enrich_lookup is a spend action; cap.spawn_researcher is a delegate action), giving a base inherent tier of high, and the autonomy modifier applies on every path because the agent is A4_fully_autonomous, can spawn agents, and has no step or runtime ceiling, pushing inherent to critical in each case. No control in the design carries status declared or verified: the six controls that would narrow or sever these paths (spend cap, step/retry limit, spawn depth limit, quota alert, permanent-failure classification, credential isolation) are all missing_recommended and earn no residual credit under rubric section 5, so residual equals inherent at critical for all three findings. With nothing currently constraining the paths, the forecast cannot be driven higher by any trigger in this document; it remains critical. The single highest-leverage fix is a structural, independent spend cap and step/retry ceiling on cap.enrich_lookup and cap.spawn_researcher (ctrl.spend_cap, ctrl.step_limit): if implemented and shown to make the sink unreachable regardless of model behavior, residual on F1 and F2 would drop to low under step 1; short of that, it still earns step-3 credit and meaningfully lowers the tier.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided; capability scope for cap.enrich_lookup and cap.spawn_researcher (especially credential_scope on cap.spawn_researcher and cap.crm_write) is inferred from prose and marked unknown or conservatively estimated where not stated.

No governance or approval documentation was provided; the complete absence of controls is taken at face value from the runtime notes rather than independently verified against the live system configuration.
Line-level citations into 'runtime notes' use bullet order from the artifact as given, since no line numbers were provided for that artifact.
